requirements.text: The ZNIX Framework must provide a centralized store for user information.
The ZNIX Framework must provide a hierarchical model for managing information, including inheritance and association-based relationships.
The ZNIX Framework must allow users to add, remove, modify, and back up information without disrupting the hierarchy.
The ZNIX Framework must provide a public API for developing ZNIX-aware client applications.
The ZNIX Framework must include a proxy mechanism to enable ZNIX-unaware applications to utilize framework capabilities.
The system must support data capturing from Outlook Express 6.0, Outlook 2003, Address Book 6.0, Internet Explorer 6.0, Opera 7.5, Firefox 1.0, and Word 2003.
The system must provide a browser GUI for navigating the information hierarchy.
The system must maintain a residue in the data store when information is archived to removable media to indicate the archive's existence.
The ZNIX Framework must run on systems with at least 256 megabytes of RAM.
The Framework Shell must not utilize more than 40 megabytes of RAM.
The Mean Time Between Failure (MTBF) must exceed 3 months.
The GUI must be designed for users with basic IT skills, mimicking popular Windows applications.
The Framework must guard against malicious scripts on remote websites accessing its information.
The Framework must guard against unintended corruption of information by the user.
The Framework must operate in single-user mode with no networking capabilities.
The system must be compatible with Windows 2000 Professional and Windows XP.
The system must conform to ISO 10646 (Unicode UTF-8) standards for character set encoding.
The ZNIX Framework must be licensed under the GNU Library General Public License (LGPL).
The browser and associated tools must be licensed under the GNU Public License (GPL).
